assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.

The requested period is 17 Sep 2026, compared with 16 Sep 2026 (the immediately preceding period of equal length). The detailed analysis uses a wider window, 17-18 Sep against a 10-16 Sep baseline, because the anomaly spans both days.
caveats: The comparison window covers 17-18 Sep, because the incident continued into 18 Sep. The question asked about 17 Sep, so figures for the window include 18 Sep.
The 716 excess failed attempts and 2,229 affected attempts are measured against a reference rate of 86.87% for Kestrel Bank card methods in 10-16 Sep.
The hour-of-day view mixes all acquirers and is noisy at low volumes. The acquirer-level and hourly Kestrel views are better evidence for timing.

facts.text: Across 17-18 Sep the overall attempt success rate was 86.98% on 22,790 attempts, versus 90.07% on 83,268 attempts in the 10-16 Sep baseline. That is a 3.1pp fall, and it is statistically and practically significant.
The daily series flags 17-18 Sep as a drop window. The lowest day was 18 Sep at 86.66%, against a median daily rate of 89.72%.

The drop is concentrated in one acquirer. Kestrel Bank's success rate fell 11.54pp, from 90.03% to 78.49%. Northstar Bank (-0.44pp), Meridian Bank (+0.27pp) and Saffron Bank (+0.24pp) showed no significant change.

Within Kestrel Bank, only card methods were affected. Debit card fell 30.11pp (86.42% to 56.31%), credit card fell 28.71pp (88.64% to 59.94%) and card EMI fell 23.87pp (80.67% to 56.8%). UPI, wallet and netbanking showed no significant change.
For Kestrel Bank card methods, the ACQ_TIMEOUT failure code rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
Across all traffic, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.08 to 3.58 per 100 attempts (815 failures in the current window). It is the only failure code with a meaningful increase.

The hourly timeline for Kestrel Bank card methods shows the problem running from 2026-09-17 10:00 to 2026-09-18 22:00, about 36 hours. The worst hour was 2026-09-18 02:00, with a 36.36% success rate against a reference of 86.87%.
Impact on Kestrel Bank card methods: 2,229 attempts were affected, with about 716 excess failed attempts compared with the reference rate.
The data-quality scan found no issues (0 findings) for the window.

response.headline: Yes. An incident hit card payments routed through Kestrel Bank from about 10:00 on 17 Sep and continued through 18 Sep. Overall success rate fell 3.1pp, from 90.07% to 86.98%, versus the 10-16 Sep baseline.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check with Kestrel Bank and Paysight's own routing and monitoring logs for incident notices, latency or timeout alerts, and the exact start and recovery times around 17 Sep 10:00 and 18 Sep 22:00.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is isolated to one acquirer and to its card methods. Failures are almost entirely ACQ_TIMEOUT, a technical acquirer-side timeout code. Customer drop-off, issuer declines and risk declines did not rise. Other acquirers and Kestrel's UPI, wallet and netbanking were unaffected.
hypotheses.text: A technical problem on the Kestrel Bank acquiring side, such as connectivity or processing degradation for card transactions, caused the incident.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A technical problem on the Kestrel Bank acquiring side, such as connectivity or processing degradation for card transactions, caused the incident.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence points to an acquirer-side timeout issue, but only the acquirer or routing logs can confirm it.
recommendations.text: Confirm the root cause and the recovery time with Kestrel Bank, and get an incident report covering 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: For Kestrel Bank card methods, the ACQ_TIMEOUT failure code rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
recommendations.rationale: The incident ran for about 36 hours and caused about 716 excess failed attempts on Kestrel Bank card methods. Faster detection and re-routing would shorten such events.
recommendations.text: Set up an alert on ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts for each acquirer and payment method, and review failover or re-routing of card traffic away from a degraded acquirer.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Impact on Kestrel Bank card methods: 2,229 attempts were affected, with about 716 excess failed attempts compared with the reference rate.
recommendations.rationale: Failed card attempts on Kestrel Bank in this window were technical failures, so some of those customers may still be recoverable.
recommendations.text: Review affected merchants for retry or recovery options, such as prompting customers to retry or offering UPI as an alternative, for failed card attempts in the window.
